one_liner: Senior Executive Service director running DOJ's entire library system and museum, setting strategy, budgets, policy and modernization through two subordinate assistant directors.
fit_summary: Daniel, this is an SES role that requires extensive executive leadership of complex library, museum, archival or knowledge-management organizations plus GS-1410 librarian qualifications, which nothing in your known background shows. Your IEM consulting and policy knowledge could touch ECQ1 and stakeholder work, but you likely cannot meet MTQ 1-3 or the librarian education standard. Treat this as a posting to skip unless you have unlisted library or museum leadership experience.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens or nationals); veterans' preference does not apply to the SES.
Must meet GS-1410 Librarian professional qualifications: library science education (an MLS/MLIS is generally expected) or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
Must show progressively responsible executive leadership directly related to all 3 MTQs, including leading subordinate managers in a library, museum, archival or knowledge-management organization.
Top Secret clearance and background investigation, drug screening, OGE 278 financial disclosure, and Selective Service registration if applicable.
If selected, you also need certification by an OPM Qualifications Review Board before appointment.
strategy: First, honestly check whether you have led library, museum, archival or knowledge-management programs with managers reporting to you; if not, skip this posting and save your effort.

Instead, target GS-0301, GS-0089 (emergency management), program analyst, or legislative and intergovernmental affairs roles at FEMA, DHS, or Virginia VDEM. These better match your IEM and policy background.
If you still apply, fit the ECQs and MTQs into a strict 2-page resume with dates and scope. Add concrete results only where they are true, such as size of budgets, teams and programs.
Frame IEM work around any knowledge-management, records, plan-library or digital information systems you built for government clients, if that actually happened.
Submit before 11:59pm EST on 11/11/2026, and include transcripts showing any library science coursework.
resume_bullets: Led [number]-person team delivering [knowledge-management/records/digitization project] for [government client], managing a $[budget] contract and achieving [result].
Developed [policy/plan/framework] adopted by [agency/jurisdiction], coordinating [number] stakeholder organizations to [outcome].
Directed modernization of [information system or document repository] for [client], improving [access/search/retrieval metric] by [amount].
interview_questions: Describe a time you set strategic direction for a complex information organization and led subordinate managers to deliver it.
How have you used digitization or new technology to improve access to collections or institutional knowledge?
Tell us about defending a budget and cutting waste while protecting mission priorities.
How would you balance resources between the Library and Museum programs?
watch_outs: Requires senior executive experience leading library or museum organizations, which you do not appear to have.
Librarian (GS-1410) qualification standard effectively expects an MLS/MLIS or equivalent.
Top Secret clearance, OGE 278 disclosure and OPM QRB review add time and scrutiny.
The resume is limited to 2 pages and must still cover 5 ECQs and 3 MTQs.
